description: Orange stone forked with white light. It hums in sunlight, and no creature yet has answered for it.
lore: The hum is not audible across a room and never has been. It is in the hand, and only in sun: carry one into shade and it stops inside a breath, take it out and it is back before your fingers close. Two hundred and fifty gold, orange plates forked through with white. In a weapon it burns, and it burns worst at whatever has been longest out of the light.

A man on the western roads has carried one for forty years. He does not fight with it and has never had it set. The pocket has been re-sewn nine times and the stone is exactly as it was the day he was paid it — a stone cannot be forgotten, so it cannot wear, so it outlasts the patience of the man carrying it by a margin that does not bear working out. He takes work that moves. A man who stays where he is meets what comes past him; a man who keeps going meets more.

What he is waiting for is whatever this came out of, and he has a description ready and no evidence for any of it: something that stands out in the open at the top of the day, something that hums. He has never heard it anywhere but in his own hand. Asked what he means to do if it is ever in front of him, he does not say break it. He says he will do it [[lore/the_waking|the courtesy]] — sit down a little way off, ask its name and one true thing. He knows how that sounds. He has known for forty years and has not changed the answer.
gm_notes: Unbound: the carrier's creature is his belief and nothing in the record supports it — his description is assembled backwards from the stone, and the text says so. The courtesy turned on an animal is the point of the leaf; he is not a crank, he is doing the only thing this country knows how to do with something that has no telling. Do not let a later writer hand him the animal.
